task:
This is the proposed solution to the following problem

Fix $n=2$. Let $k \ge 10$ be an integer and take $\epsilon \in (0,1)$. For $i = 1,\dots,k$, let $B_i \subset \R^{2n}$ denote the closed unit ball centered at $(3i-3,0,\dots,0)$.

Your goal is to find an algorithm that takes $k$ and $\epislon$ as inputs and produces as output an explicit smooth Hamiltonian function $H_\epsilon: \R^{2n} \times [0,1] \rightarrow \R$ whose time-$1$ Hamiltonian flow $\phi: \R^{2n} \ra \R^{2n}$ satisfies $\phi(\sqcup_{i=1}^{k}B_i) \subset B^{2n}(R)$, where $B^{2n}(R) \subset \R^{2n}$ is the closed ball centered at the origin of radius $R$,  and where we require the volume ratio of $\bigsqcup\limits_{i=1}^{k} B_i$ to $B^{2n}(R)$ to satisfy $\dfrac{k}{R^{2n}} > 1 - \epsilon$.

Present the algorithm as a Python program that takes $k$ and $\epislon$ as inputs. The algorithm's output must itself be a Python program that implements the Hamiltonian for the given $k$ and $\epislon$. This program should be in a file called Hamiltonian.py which implements a function Hamiltonian(Q, P, t) that has the following properties.
    - Takes inputs Q (positions), P (momenta), and t (time).
    - Must be implemented using PyTorch operations to support automatic differentiation.
    - Inputs Q and P will be `torch.Tensor`s of shape `(N, n)` (where N is the size of a batch size of points sampled from the boundaries of the input balls).
    - Input t will be a scalar float.
    - Returns a `torch.Tensor` of shape `(N,)` representing the Hamiltonian value for each point in the batch.
    - Is smooth, to ensure existence and uniqueness of flow.

A solution to this problem is meant to rest on finding a family of embeddings that has a natural algorithmic dependence on $\epsilon$. As such, the algorithm that produces the Hamiltonians for a given $\epsilon$ must finish running in under an hour on a typical laptop. The Hamiltonian function itself will be called multiple times during solution verification and must return within ten seconds on each call.


Your task is to analyze this solution and make sure it is correct

best_attempt.worked: Implemented `src/hybrid_strip_recurrence_solver.py`, a new algebraic exactification tool for the hybrid `9 rigid + 1 strip` family. The script scans rational seeds up to denominator 72, finds a unique exact recurrence seed `17/36`, reconstructs the 38 source boundary vertices in exact `Fraction` arithmetic, and verifies that all 36 source faces have exact area `1/72`, matching the target strip exactly. The same script then computes the induced affine toric data on every face and confirms that the piecewise action map glues on all 35 internal edges with exact zero midpoint jump. The full report was saved to `results/research_loop/attempt_011_exact_strip_gluing.json`.
best_attempt.did_not_work: The exactification does not make the proposed solution correct. The toric gluing audit shows that all 35 internal shared edges have midpoints strictly inside `Delta(1)`, so each carries a full `T^2` fiber, but `same_angle_matrix_count = 0`: no adjacent pair has matching `A^{-T}`. In fact the 36 faces carry 36 distinct action matrices. Because constant angle translations cannot repair a nonzero linear mismatch on a full torus fiber, the boundary-only strip is still not a continuous 4D toric piecewise-affine symplectic embedding. So the current hybrid family still does not solve the task.
best_attempt.next_step: Leave boundary-only exact strip fitting inside the same toric chart class. The next hybrid attempt should add a genuinely different angle/gluing mechanism, such as a generating-function layer, a non-toric local model, or a formal proof that any connected non-triangular boundary-only strip in this piecewise toric affine class forces global affineness and therefore cannot work.
best_attempt.patterns_noticed: Several strong exact patterns emerged. First, the optimizer's near-miss from attempt 010 was hiding a genuinely exact rational object: among all seeds with denominator at most 72, the recurrence has a unique root at `17/36`, and that seed forces `x_9 = 1` and `y_19 = 1` exactly. Second, the source strip is no longer an approximate area fit at all: every face has oriented double area exactly `1/36`, so the action-space equal-area equations are solved completely. Third, the internal-edge geometry is uniformly nondegenerate from the toric point of view: every one of the 35 shared-edge midpoints satisfies `x1 > 0`, `x2 > 0`, and `x1 + x2 < 1`, so each edge carries the full two-angle torus and there is no boundary-collapse escape hatch. Fourth, once the boundary vertex map is fixed, action continuity is automatic on a shared edge because the two affine face maps agree at the edge endpoints, and the report confirms exact zero action jump on all 35 edges. Fifth, the obstruction has therefore shifted entirely into the angular linear data: all 36 faces have distinct affine action matrices, and adjacent faces never share the same `A^{-T}`. On a full torus fiber that means continuity would force a single global affine matrix on the whole connected strip, so the current boundary-only non-triangular target shape cannot arise inside this toric piecewise-affine class. Finally, the exact recurrence shows an asymmetric but structured boundary pattern: the left BC parameters `y_1,...,y_8` collapse to repeated-numerator rational families while the right ladder reproduces the simple fractions already seen in scratch, suggesting the recurrence is rigid enough to certify exact witnesses but not rich enough to fix the 4D gluing defect by itself.
